intent: Help the student see that 13 ones can be regrouped into 1 ten and 3 ones using base-ten blocks.

data.title: Trading Blocks with Place Value
data.description: Learn how blocks can be traded between columns to show the same value in different ways.

challenges.instruction: Look at the blocks on your mat and predict what will happen when you trade.
challenges.hint: Think about what happens when you take one hundred and break it into tens.

challenges.instruction: Examine the current blocks and make your prediction before trading.
challenges.hint: Remember that one ten can be traded for ten ones.

challenges.instruction: Study the blocks displayed and predict the outcome of the next trade.
challenges.hint: Check the tens place and see how many ones you will get.

challenges.instruction: Look closely at the mat and predict the new block counts.
challenges.hint: Count your hundreds carefully before making a trade.

judgement.reasoning: The student wrote 513 for 37 + 26 because they do not regroup 13 ones into 1 ten and 3 ones. The generator was instructed to address trading 13 ones into 1 ten and 3 ones, but instead generated high-number regrouping challenges involving 3-digit numbers (550, 622, 215, 435) focusing on decomposing/unbundling (breaking hundreds into tens or tens into ones, as hints indicate) rather than bundling 10 ones into a ten.
judgement.verdict: A teacher would not use this detour because it deals with decomposing 3-digit numbers rather than composing 10 ones into 1 ten to fix the 13 ones obstacle.
